analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The source text of LM2 Torah 56 introduces four key concepts — לֵב יִשְׂרְאֵלִי (Jewish heart), הָאֱלֹקוּת (Divinity), מָקוֹם (place), and מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם (Place of the World, a name for God) — none of which appear in bechina-typed edges for this Torah, since there are none in the dataset. The text's central move is: (1) Divinity resides in the heart (כִּי הָאֱלֹקוּת הוּא בַּלֵּב); (2) God is called 'the Place of the World' (מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם) — He contains the world but is not contained by it; (3) therefore one who has a Jewish heart is similarly not constrained by any particular place, because the infinite Place dwells within him. This is a theological syllogism, not a bechina mapping. The word 'הוּא' in 'הוּא מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם' is used in its predicative sense (identifying what God is called), not as a bechina equating formula between two separate concepts. There is no instance of the text saying 'X הוּא בְּחִינַת Y' or 'X נִקְרָא Y' (where X and Y are distinct thematic concepts being mapped to each other as parallel aspects). The relationship between לֵב and הָאֱלֹקוּת is one of indwelling and containment, not of shared essential nature — Divinity dwells inside the heart, it does not share the same nature as the heart. Therefore no gap additions can be proposed: there are no packages into which additions could be placed, and no bechina formulations in the source text that would constitute missing package nodes.
